item.title: 3 dead after NBC Los Angeles news helicopter crashes in Chatsworth
item.description: The crash happened near the spot of a deadly Metro bus crash in Chatsworth.

item.title: White House backs Hegseth as new details come out about Iran war's cost
item.description: The Iran war has cost the U.S. military at least $33.4 billion — most of it on munitions — and not including hundreds of millions more spent by other agencies, the Pentagon says.

item.title: Coast Guard, FBI boarded Texas-bound oil tanker to investigate cyberattack
item.description: The U.S. has so far not attributed the potential breach to a specific actor, but Iranian state media amplified the story in the weeks following the attack.

item.title: House votes to limit Trump's power to strike Iran for 3rd time
item.description: The previous votes have failed to stop President Trump from waging war with Iran.

item.title: Blanche says "of course" White House will comply with Supreme Court decision on mail ballots
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche told CBS News' Ed O'Keefe on Tuesday "of course" the White House will comply with a Supreme Court decision that keeps in place a lower court ruling that blocked the U.S. Postal Service from enforcing new regulations for mail voting.

item.title: Extended Interview: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks with CBS News' Aidan Stretch about the state of the war, Russia's recent escalation, U.S. support and more.

item.title: DOJ accuses Russian intel agents of plotting to murder U.S.-based dissident
item.description: The Justice Department is accusing several members of Russia's intelligence services of running a "global assassination network" that targeted Kremlin critics.

item.title: Stocks dive ahead of expected Fed interest rate hike
item.description: Stocks stayed in the red on Tuesday ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. CBS News contributor Javier David has a preview of the meeting.

item.title: Where AI legislation, government regulations stand
item.description: The growing concerns over AI safety brought together two people from opposite sides of the political spectrum on Tuesday: Sen. Bernie Sanders and former Trump adviser Steve Bannon. Washington Post tech reporter Gerrit De Vynk joins CBS News to discuss where AI legislation stands.

item.title: Details on arrest of 21-year-old man for alleged ISIS-inspired "mass casualty attack" plot
item.description: A 21-year-old Pennsylvania man has been arrested for allegedly plotting what could have been a "mass casualty attack" inspired by ISIS, federal officials say. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Legal expert explains Supreme Court's decision to block Trump's mail-in voting rules
item.description: The Supreme Court has struck down tighter mail-in voting regulations championed by President Trump ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. CBS News' legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks it down.

item.title: Delaware voters head to polls in last national primary before midterms
item.description: Delaware voters are heading to the polls on Tuesday in the nation's final primary election before midterms. CBS News' executive director of elections and surveys, Anthony Salvanto, breaks it down.

item.title: U.S. to spend $2 billion to $3 billion per month on Iran war, Congressional Budget Office says
item.description: The United States has spent $38 billion on the Iran war and will continue to spend billions monthly, according to a new report from the Congressional Budget Office. CBS News' Eleanor Watson has more.

item.title: Blanche defends Trump's comments on Supreme Court after it rejects new mail-in voting restrictions
item.description: President Trump called the Supreme Court's refusal to enforce stricter mail-in voting rules a "big loss" for Republicans and Americans on Tuesday, claiming it will lead to cheating. A Brookings Institute analysis found just four cases of mail voter fraud for every 10 million ballots cast in 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2022. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Sanders, Bannon call for AI regulations as fears of dangerous "superintelligence" grow
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon are both pushing the Trump administration to regulate artificial intelligence as industry leaders warn of risks to humanity. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns has more.

item.title: Delaware holds U.S. Senate primary and more races to watch today
item.description: Delaware Sen. Chris Coons is seeking a third full term.

item.title: Board votes to close Kennedy Center immediately for renovations, source says
item.description: Earlier Tuesday, a federal judge again blocked the board from adding President Trump's name to the facade of the building.

item.title: Father and daughter pilots happen to cross paths over air traffic control
item.description: Just before taking off for Munich, Germany, United Airlines pilot Kent Katnik, checked in with the tower and heard his daughter, Kenny Katnik, herself a pilot, about to take off for Syracuse. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: New photos show widespread damage at U.S. positions caused by Iranian attacks
item.description: The images were sent to CBS News by active service members under condition of anonymity.

item.title: In Washington, unlikely bedfellows like Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon talk about making AI "humans first"
item.description: As AI CEOs call for a slowdown, President Trump wants acceleration. But the issue is gaining bipartisan momentum.

item.title: Trump admin. will comply with mail ballot ruling by Supreme Court, Blanche says
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday blocked the Postal Service from enforcing new mail voting rules ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Ed Sheeran's supporting acts pull out of tour after Macklemore was dropped
item.description: Aaron Rowe, Beoga, Lukas Graham and Finneas all released statements Tuesday on Instagram saying they were withdrawing from Ed Sheeran's tour.

item.title: 9/15: CBS Evening News
item.description: FBI stops an alleged ISIS-inspired attack; Kennedy Center to close amid a Trump battle.

item.title: House panel recommends holding Leon Black in contempt in Epstein probe
item.description: The billionaire investor defied subpoenas to testify to the committee and produce nondisclosure agreements.

item.title: Own a car? You're getting socked by higher prices, and not only for gas
item.description: Car ownership costs have soared 50% since 2020, according to new economic data. Here's where motorists are getting dinged.

item.title: 9/15: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump slams Supreme Court for blocking Postal Service rules for mail ballots; Congress reacts to AI safety warnings.

item.title: Sanders says potential danger of AI is "probably greater" than nuclear weapons
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders is one of the most vocal opponents in Congress on rapid AI development, but bipartisan concerns are growing.

item.title: Ukrainian president tells CBS News Russia targeted his plane with drones
item.description: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia targeted his plane with drones as part of a campaign to intimidate him and other foreign leaders.

item.title: ICE deportees in Africa describe being stranded "on the other side of the world"
item.description: CBS News traveled to Liberia to speak to some of the Latin American deportees banished to Africa under President Trump's immigration crackdown.

item.title: 9/13: Sunday Morning
item.description: Hosted by Jane Pauley. Featured: America's missile arsenal; Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on the development of AI; fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg; testing the ethical boundaries of surrogacy; uncovering a Holocaust survival story; the allure of shipwrecks; and the annual Pumpkin Festival in Morton, Ill.
